# Asset Inventory — Electric Tile Challenge 3D

All assets in this repository are **original works generated for this project**
(mitigation of licensing risk: zero third-party assets are shipped).

## Textures (`assets/textures/`, generated by `scripts-dev/gen_textures.py`)

| File | Size | Purpose | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `tile_face.png` | 512x512 | Tile top face | glowing border ring + circuit traces; used as albedo **and** emission map |
| `floor_metal.png` | 512x512 | Arena floor | panel seams + rivets, triplanar-mapped |
| `wall_panel.png` | 1024x1024 | Arena walls | bevel frame, grooves, accent slot, vertical gradient |
| `hazard.png` | 256x256 | Grid border frame | 45° warning stripes |
| `pad_start.png` | 512x512 | Start pad | green ring + chevrons (emissive) |
| `pad_finish.png` | 512x512 | Finish pad | gold ring + checkered flag (emissive) |

Regenerate deterministically: `python3 scripts-dev/gen_textures.py`
(numpy + stdlib only; no PIL).

## Audio (`assets/audio/`, generated by `scripts-dev/gen_audio.py`)

SFX (44.1 kHz 16-bit mono WAV):

`ui_click, ui_back, step, jump, land, tile_show, tile_good, seq_note, zap,
fail, warn, go, count, star, unlock` (win maps to `unlock` — victory riser)

Music loops: `music_menu.wav` (7.6 s), `music_game.wav` (15 s) — loop mode is
enabled at runtime by `AudioManager` (`AudioStreamWAV.LOOP_FORWARD`).

Regenerate: `python3 scripts-dev/gen_audio.py` (numpy + stdlib only).

## In-engine procedural assets (GDScript)

| Asset | File | What |
|---|---|---|
| Robot character | `scripts/game/robot_model.gd` | ~25-part stylized droid: capsule limbs, sphere joints, emissive visor/core, antenna; 5 animation states |
| Arena | `scripts/game/arena.gd` | room shell, trims, columns, MultiMesh ribs, pads, Label3D signage |
| Tiles | `scripts/game/tile.gd` | emissive tile mesh + shared reveal materials |
| Sparks/confetti | `scripts/game/sparks.gd` | pooled CPU particle emitters |

## Why procedural instead of Blender/GLB (and the upgrade path)

The plan requested Blender-authored GLB assets. This build ships a fully
procedural, original stylized asset set so that:

- every asset is reproducible from committed code (no binary provenance risk),
- the repository stays tiny and reviewable,
- the visual identity is consistent and tuned for mobile (emissive neon).

The gameplay/UI architecture is decoupled from the visual source. To adopt
Blender GLB assets later: export GLB models with animations, place them under
`assets/models/`, and replace the construction calls in `robot_model.gd` /
`arena.gd` with `AnimatedMesh3D`/`AnimationPlayer` instancing — nothing else
in the game needs to change.
